correctness.rationale: Legendre identity v2(C(2r,r))=s2(r) plus binary digit subadditivity gives a unique lowest-valuation term for each odd n. The recurrence splits off the final term for n=2 mod4, where its valuation is at least one larger. All boundaries are explicit; exact checker compared 768 qualifying n up to 1024.

The proof yields strictly greater sharpness on three natural congruence classes, rather than merely renaming an established identity. Residual risk remains from other unlocated work.

value.rationale: Sharp valuations of a natural, already studied binomial congruence sum are established on three out of every four indices, with binary-digit complexity controlling the exact answer. These infinitely many and density-3/4 cases are naturally distinguished by dominance versus cancellation; the information is stronger than the original general divisibility bound and suitable for modular refinements.
